nary_nodes.label: European heatwave
evidence: France has said it recorded an increase of more than 2,000 deaths during the last week of a record-breaking European heatwave in June as forecasters warn of further extreme temperatures on the continent in the next few days.
Temperatures reached almost 40C in parts of the country, with most of the deaths reported in the south and east of the Netherlands where temperatures were highest.
Unprecedented heat in the Netherlands last week led to about 480 excess deaths, Dutch authorities said on Thursday - most of whom were aged 80 and older.

nary_nodes.label: Wildfires in Europe
evidence: Nearly 7,000 fires had broken out since the start of the summer season, with about 8,700 hectares burned so far.

Météo-France has issued red alerts for Friday and Saturday for forest fires in the southern part of the country, warning that weather conditions meant the risk of an outbreak was 'very high' compared to summer norms.

type_definitions.definition: A nation with its own government, occupying a defined territory.
A large area of land that is separated from other areas by oceans or seas.
A person who is involved in politics, especially one who holds or seeks public office.
A large human settlement, typically with a fixed boundary and a local government.
A period of time, typically 30 or 31 days, used to divide the year into smaller units.
A specific point in time, typically represented by a day, month, and year.

relation_definitions.definition: To have gone through or undergone a particular event or situation.
To have been influenced or impacted by something, often in a negative way.
To have said or expressed something, often in a formal or official capacity.
To have made something happen or exist, often as a result of a particular action or set of circumstances.
To have attained a specific temperature, often as a result of a particular weather pattern or event.
To have documented or measured something, often in an official or formal capacity.
To be related to or concerned with something, often in a general or abstract sense.
